core_obligations: Part (1): combine flatness of the module with the base change lemma and the identification of the base-changed module as a localisation of the tensor product (proof lines 24425-24431).

Part (2): assume the base-changed module flat and the base flat, tensor an injection with the base, localise, and use flatness of the base-changed module to conclude the original module is flat (proof lines 24432-24453), with the statements about ring maps following as special cases.
proof_roadmap: Get the forward direction from base change plus localisation (proof lines 24425-24431).
Descend flatness along the local diagram (proof lines 24432-24454).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in a local commutative diagram where one ring is a localisation of a tensor product, flatness of a module passes to its base change, and conversely descends when the base map is flat, with the corresponding statements for flat ring maps as special cases (statement lines 24401-24423). The proof does not chase Tor: it identifies the base-changed module as a localisation of the tensor product, obtains the forward direction from the base change lemma, and in the other direction tensors an injection with the flat base, localises, and uses flatness of the base-changed module to conclude (proof lines 24425-24454). Recognising the base-changed module as a localisation is the step that makes both directions accessible. H2.
